note: The vocabulary: every slot the Master Spec defines. Which slots are REQUIRED is a separate file (profiles/*.json) because that changes for business reasons, not technical ones. Coarse first: sections a Baseline populates carry full slot detail; the rest carry kind and source so the engine can be built against the whole shape. Content passes continue.

labelRules.note: A label can never be upgraded by a later step. Acceptance means a human agreed with the sentence, not that the fact changed origin. 'documented' requires a cited record.

naReasonLabels.note: Which honesty label an `na` reason reads as IN A CLIENT'S DOCUMENT. Increment 4 Amendment 1 §B. This lives here rather than in the field config because an honesty label is a claim the BINDER makes about what kind of knowing a statement rests on. The field app makes no such claim — it records that a concierge chose a reason. Deciding that `no-access` reads as Not accessible TO A HOMEOWNER is a binder-voice decision, and pushing it into the field config would put a downstream concern on a session that cannot validate it.
naReasonLabels.defaultNote: An unmapped reason is NOT an error. It defaults to `not-inspected` and is reported, never refused. The asymmetry is the whole point: 'we did not inspect it' is true of every gap in the report, while 'we could not reach it' additionally claims we tried and were blocked. A reason defaulting to `not-accessible` would put a claim about the visit into a client's document that nobody made. Fail open, in the honest direction.
naReasonLabels.scopeNote: Only the honesty CLASS comes from here. Membership in the gap list still comes from the config's own `feedsGapList` boolean, and the row's words still come from the config's own `label`. A fifth gap-feeding reason therefore needs no code change and no entry here — it feeds the list, speaks in its own label, and reads as not-inspected until the design session decides it earns otherwise.
naReasonLabels.recorded: Whether `deferred` should eventually carry a label of its own is recorded, not specced. It defaults to not-inspected today, which is true, and its reason line already says 'Deferred to visit two'. Revisit with the slot mapping, not before.

slotKinds.record-set: Repeating records. Complete when every entity implied by the property's own triggers has a record.
slotKinds.coverage: A defined list; each item present | confirmed-absent | not-found. Complete when every applicable item has a state.
slotKinds.derived: Computed from other sections. Never independently missing.
slotKinds.narrative: Free prose, unbounded. Never 'complete' — only empty or started. Never appears in a gap report.

slots.bindingRule: RECONCILED against Checklist Master v1.6.2. **The field checklist already declares the binding.** 36 items carry `satisfy: pin <type>` — utl.main-shutoff is literally 'Main water shutoff pinned, photographed wide, tagged'. So a §1 item binds by `pinnedBy` (the field item id that requires the pin) plus `viaItems` (the component items carrying the shutoff detail). Where no zone item pins it, componentType alone is the binding. **Do not re-derive which component satisfies which §1 entry — the field master owns that, and §1 is now its standing acceptance test.**
slots.zoneIndependence: **Resolved in master v1.6.2 — this was the largest defect found since G1.** The `utl.*` mechanical items previously lived in the `utility` zone list, so a house with its mechanicals in an open basement corner produced an **empty shutoff map** if the concierge created a `basement` zone. Now: every mechanical item lives in **`mechanical-base`**, inherited by all 13 zone types and gated at list level on **`zone.has_mechanicals`**. Zone type is a labelling convenience; the attribute drives content. **All ids carried through the move** — base went 33→57 and zone 76→52, 109 both sides, so 'moved, not duplicated' is verifiable. **§1 binding by item id is therefore unaffected.**
slots.sessionAttestation: `ses.shutoff-map` (session, core, action) — a human attestation that the §1 map is complete house-wide, every entry pinned or explicitly recorded absent. **The builder audits the same thing independently. When the two disagree, surface it** — one is wrong and neither is authoritative over the other.

inheritanceRule: Declared in the master as ``### `child` — inherits `parent` ``; the child's rendered list is the parent's items followed by its own, and ids stay globally unique. **A binding target matches a type OR any descendant** — a water-softener pin satisfies a water-treatment expectation. 11 relations as of v1.5.1.
triggerVocabularyRule: RECONCILED against Checklist Master v1.6.2 §3. FOUR namespaces: `property.*` (Table A, now 17 flags, declared at intake before the visit) · `zone.*` (Table B) · `pin.*` (a pin of this type in THIS zone — zone-scoped strictly, rejected by the validator at session scope) · `house.*` (v1.6 — a pin of this type ANYWHERE in this visit). **Neither pin nor house is a superset of the other:** the zone form under-fires a house question, the house form over-fires a zone one. Maintenance-schedule conditions are house-scoped. `answer.*` is permanently absent from the field config and belongs to the builder — see §answerConditions.
componentVocabularyRule: RECONCILED 2026-07-27 against Checklist Master v1.6.2 — 58 component types, 11 inheritance relations, 23 `.unit` items. **Table F asserts nothing retired in v1.6.x.** Ten stubs excluded from expectations: ev-charger, cistern, elevator-lift, outbuilding, radon-fan, backflow-preventer, boiler-zone-valve, appliance-freezer, iron-filter. `dock` is filled (was a stub actively referenced by `sit.shoreline`).
answerConditions: **Conditions on a recorded value are the builder's, permanently.** The field app cannot evaluate half the inputs — a radon result arrives three months later, a permit date comes from a document. So the builder holds every answer (field, lab, document), evaluates the condition, and emits the resulting item as a carried item in the session plan. No new field machinery; it uses the round trip that already exists. Form: `answer.<itemId> <op> <value>` — `answer.utl.drain-material-id in (clay, orangeburg)` for the §13 sewer-camera trigger, `answer.fc.width > 5`. **Choice option values are therefore the builder's condition vocabulary: renaming or removing one is a breaking change here, not a content edit** (master §9).
listGateRule: v1.6.2 dialect: a list heading may carry `— gated on <ref>`, conditioning every item in it. Where an item also has a trigger cell, the effective condition is **allOf(list gate, item trigger)** — the cell's own `|` stays anyOf internally. **The evaluator must compose both**, or every Fuel item (`has_mechanicals` AND `property.gas`) fires in every zone.
retirementLineage: Master Table F records retired id, version, successors and reason as structured data. **Software must not use it to join a series** — a retired id stays a discontinuity. Read it only to show a person where a broken series continued.
vocabularyCrossCheckRule: Every trigger referenced must appear in `triggerVocabulary` under its own namespace, and `property.*` must match Checklist Master Table A exactly. `house.*` and `pin.*` must name a declared component type; `zone.*` a Table B attribute. **Validate against the master's declared vocabulary, not only internal consistency** — a transformation applied uniformly to ids and to every reference leaves everything agreeing with everything and everything wrong. **Every trigger used must be declared; a declared flag need not be used. The component-type half is evaluated per import against that import's own config snapshot — never against a checked-in copy, which goes stale and produces false positives. Fail open on an unrecognised name.**
reconciledAgainst: CHECKLIST-MASTER v1.11 (2026-07-28). 409 items, 61 component types (plus 9 stubs with ids reserved and no items), 8 retirement-lineage rows.
tableI_provenance: v1.9–v1.11 Table I: any value transcribed from a physical artifact names the photo item that captures it. **The builder must carry the declaration, not just the value.** A value whose source photo item resolved `na / none-present` is **unverifiable** and must stay distinguishable from a verified one at every layer — including a fleet or registry view. Provenance is **co-visibility on the same pin**, resolved across component inheritance, not global existence of the item.
parsingWarning: **Escaped pipes.** Table cells use `\|` inside choice and multi-alternative pin values — `choice (ball\|gate\|other)`, `pin \`comparison-position\|dock\``. A naive cell split drops every such row silently: it cost this schema a phantom 'stale id' report and a month of a wrong item count. Neutralise `\|` before splitting. Field's v1.7 rule bans markdown emphasis in parsed cells for the same class of reason.
countingNote: **61 typed component headings, not 62.** Section 7's final `###` is `Stubs (ids reserved; items TBD)` — a section heading, not a type. Caught by Builder Code. Same class as the escaped-pipe bug and their four false findings: **a boundary assumed rather than located.** Counting rule for anyone re-deriving this: bound section 7 at `## 8`, take `###` headings carrying a backticked id, count the child only on `— inherits` lines, and treat `smoke-alarm / co-alarm` as two. Stubs have no headings of their own.
dualSourcedFacts:
**A slot may declare `preferredLabel`, and it needs more machinery than first claimed.** Some facts arrive from two sources with different honesty labels — electrical service size is `Reported` at intake and `Observed` in the field. Neither overwrites the other, and **the discrepancy is a first-class output**: an owner reporting 200A on a 100A panel is carrying a renovation assumption worth more than either number alone.

**CORRECTION (2026-07-29): the overlay model does not already do this.** Overlays hold a *history* of values resolving to one current value by recency. Two simultaneously-valid values from different sources is a different shape — **value-per-source, resolved by declared preference rather than by time.** That is a schema addition, not existing machinery, and the earlier claim otherwise was asserted without checking.

**Precedence cannot be a fixed order.** For a current-state question an observation beats a document; for a historical one the document wins, because nobody watched it happen. So the slot declares it: `preferredLabel: observed` on electrical service, `preferredLabel: documented` on install date. Generalises to year built (intake vs permit), roof age (intake vs invoice).
technologySection:
**A technology inventory takes its own section rather than a §7 subsection. One reason, not two.**

**§7's expectation set is trigger-derived; technology's is not derivable at all** — there are no `property.*` flags for a printer, and the intake question sets none. So `expectationSource: "session-attestation"`, satisfied by a session-close coverage item. A new value on an existing field, not a new slot kind.

**A transfer-package argument was previously given here and is withdrawn.** Master Spec §23 is an explicit **inclusion** list — systems inventory, service history, permits, test results, transferable warranties, capital plan. Technology is not on it, so exclusion is already the default and there is nothing to filter. *(Also: §23 has three audiences — a buyer, an executor or family member, a new caretaker or service — not two.)*

**Required:** make · model · location · how it connects · a label photograph or a declared unverifiable. **Required on network equipment:** owned-or-rented — the one field that changes who the client phones. **Optional:** serial · age · known issues. **Upstream device as free text**, never a modelled topology.

**The moveables list is a separate slot that can never be complete** — a household acquires a phone next month. Narrative treatment for gap purposes, structured for querying, `Reported by homeowner`. **How the list arrives is provenance, not design** — a written list, an emailed list, the client reading it out, a recording. Only the audio route carries transcription and extraction in its chain.

**No transcript-versus-pins reconciliation is specified.** An earlier version described one, using televisions as the example — but the inspection sees televisions, and **moveables are precisely what the inspection cannot see**, so there is largely nothing to reconcile. The general rule stands and needs no mechanism: a claim in a recording is checked against the rest of the binder like any other claim.
